title: Grouped table search
statement: Let $k,n$ be nonnegative integers, let $x$ be a finite binary input, and let $G$ be a list of groups of transition actions, each group having length $3^{k+1}$. Let $R$ be a list of remaining actions whose length is the rank $r$ of a control state, and put $A=G\mathbin{\|}R$, where $G\mathbin{\|}R$ means the groups flattened and then concatenated with $R$. Suppose a configuration $d$ is in the initial recording state, its summary tape at offset $s$ from its head contains $1$ exactly when $s<|G|$ for every $0\le s\le |G|$, and its table tape stores the bit encoding of $A$ consecutively from its head. Starting the search machine in the control state carrying rank $r$, after $T=|G|+1+\operatorname{cost}(A)$ steps it reaches the done control state, with the table and summary heads shifted forward respectively by the length of the encoding of $A$ and by $|G|$. It does not reach the done control state at any earlier time. Throughout times $u\le T$, the input-head position, tape contents, and output remain those of $d$, and every other work-tape head stays fixed.
hypotheses_covered: $d$ starts in the recording machine's initial state
summary-tape cells at offsets $0$ through $|G|$ have the stated values
table-tape cells store the encoding of $G$ flattened and followed by $R$
